newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan president says rebel leader escaped death.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan president says rebel leader escaped death.

text.p: President Yoweri Museveni has said Juma Oris, a former Uganda army colonel leading a rebel group operating in northwest Uganda, escaped from an attack in which many of his followers died.

Addressing a national youth camp at Mpigi, 60 km (40 miles) west of Kampala, on Saturday, Museveni said he had reliable reports that Oris was still alive somewhere in southern Sudan, the state-owned Sunday Vision reported.
He discounted a report in a local newspaper, The Monitor, that Oris was killed by Zairean rebels at Katambala, in northeast Zaire, after escaping from Uganda a week ago.

Oris, a close associate of dictator Idi Amin who ruled Uganda from 1971 to 1979, served as a minister in Amin's government. He fled into exile in Sudan when Amin was overthrown, returning in 1993 to head the rebel West Nile Bank Front with the aim of overthrowing Museveni.
Museveni also said the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) rebels, who have been operating over a wide area of northern Uganda, would soon be overcome.
He said the Uganda army had been reorganised, and was succeeding against the rebels.
